Case Studies

Two projects, start to finish

1 · Healthcare System Implementation: Kipu EMR & Relias LMS

I led a behavioral health outpatient program off a slow legacy EMR and manual processes onto Kipu EMR for clinical documentation and Relias LMS for staff training, owning every phase from the business case through post-go-live stabilization.

SettingBehavioral health outpatient program (OP / IOP / PHP), ~25 staff
My roleBusiness Operations & Compliance Manager; implementation lead
SystemsKipu EMR · Relias LMS
TimelineAug 2024 – Feb 2025
  1. Business Need
  2. Requirements
  3. Current / Future Workflow
  4. UAT
  5. Training
  6. Go-Live
  7. Stabilization
80+ → ~20
Open audit findings reduced (about 75%)
20
Staff trained and onboarded in Relias
15–20
UAT scenarios tested before go-live
5
KPI dashboards, the organization's first executive reporting
Phase 1

Business Need

  • The legacy EMR was slow, and intake, training tracking, and reporting were largely manual.
  • Charts were hard to audit, training compliance was hard to prove, and open audit findings had passed 80.
  • Aligned leadership on goals: audit-ready charts, trackable training compliance, and program-level reporting.
Deliverables: problem statement, success criteria.
Phase 2

Requirements

  • Gathered requirements from clinical, intake, administrative, and leadership staff.
  • Turned documentation and accreditation standards into system requirements for OP, IOP, and PHP.
  • Defined role-based training requirements for Relias.
Deliverables: requirements by stakeholder group, role-based training matrix.
Phase 3

Current-State / Future-State Workflow

Before
  • Slow legacy EMR that staff worked around
  • Manual intake, tracking, and follow-up
  • Training completion tracked by hand
  • Documentation gaps found only during audits
After
  • Standardized electronic intake and assessment in Kipu
  • Required fields and signatures built into the workflow
  • Role-based Relias assignments with completion tracking
  • System data feeding leadership KPI dashboards
Deliverables: current- and future-state process maps (referral → intake → assessment → treatment plan → notes → discharge), gap analysis.
Phase 4

User Acceptance Testing

  • Wrote 15–20 test scenarios from real workflows, such as admitting a client at each level of care and completing a discharge.
  • Ran testing with clinical and admin users, logged defects, and retested each fix.
Deliverables: UAT test cases, issue log, retesting documentation, and Clinical Director approval for go-live.
Phase 5

Training

  • Trained 20 staff with role-specific sessions for clinicians, intake and admin staff, and supervisors.
  • Set up Relias course assignments by role and tracked completion for audits.
Deliverables: training plan, quick-reference guides, role-based Relias curriculum.
Phase 6

Go-Live

  • Ran a readiness checklist covering accounts and permissions, form configuration, and support coverage.
  • Provided hands-on support in the first days and triaged issues in real time.
Deliverables: go-live checklist, cutover and escalation plan.
Phase 7

Stabilization

  • Audited charts against the new standards, refined forms from user feedback, and followed up on gaps.
  • Built 5 KPI dashboards from system data. Open audit findings fell from 80+ to about 20.
Deliverables: audit tracking, workflow refinements, KPI dashboards.

2 · Audit Turnaround: 80+ Open Findings to ~20

The same program came into my role with more than 80 open findings from state licensing, accreditation, and Medicaid/payer reviews. I traced them to their root causes, rebuilt the processes behind them, and tracked each one to closure, bringing open findings down to about 20 in 6–12 months.

Audit sourcesState licensing · Accreditation · Medicaid / payer
Finding areasClinical documentation · Personnel files · Policies · Facility & safety
My roleBusiness Operations & Compliance Manager; remediation lead
Timeframe6–12 months
Step 1

Inventory & Prioritize

  • Pulled every open finding from all three audit sources into one tracker.
  • Grouped them into four areas and ranked them by licensing and payment risk.
Step 2

Find Root Causes

  • Looked for what each group of findings had in common instead of fixing them one at a time.
  • Traced repeat problems to process gaps: no standard workflow, unclear ownership, or no way to catch misses before an audit.
Step 3

Fix the Process

  • Clinical documentation: redesigned SOPs and moved charting into Kipu with required fields (see case study 1).
  • Personnel files: standardized file checklists and moved required training into Relias.
  • Policies: updated or wrote missing policies and procedures.
  • Facility & safety: set owners and schedules for recurring requirements.
Step 4

Track to Closure

  • Assigned an owner and due date to every finding and reviewed status with leadership.
  • Ran internal reviews to confirm fixes held before the next external audit.
Deliverables: findings tracker, root-cause summary, revised SOPs and policies, corrective action plans.
